title: New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District will determine who represents the western and northern portions of the state, including cities such as Nashua, Concord, Keene, and Lebanon, in the U.S. House. First-term Democratic incumbent Maggie Goodlander, who narrowly won the open seat in 2024 with 52% of the vote, is seeking re-election in a district that has trended Democratic but remains competitive. Republicans see an opportunity to flip the seat; Lily Tang Williams, the 2024 Republican nominee who lost to Goodlander, is running again after also losing a 2022 bid. A competitive Republican primary is also emerging. Control of the U.S. House is expected to be closely divided in 2026, making every competitive race nationally significant.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the 2026 general election in NH-02 have been released as of mid-2025. Primary polling for the Democratic and Republican primaries may become available closer to the September 8, 2026 primary date.

candidates.name: Maggie Goodlander
candidates.summary: Maggie Goodlander is the first-term incumbent U.S. Representative for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. Before Congress, she served as a Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Biden Justice Department, as a foreign policy adviser to U.S. Senators John McCain and Joe Lieberman, and as counsel to the House Judiciary Committee during the first impeachment of President Donald Trump. She is focusing her re-election campaign on lowering costs, protecting health care, and standing up to the Trump administration.

candidates.name: Lily Tang Williams
candidates.summary: Lily Tang Williams is a Republican perennial candidate who has run for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District in 2022 and 2024, winning the GOP nomination in both cycles. She is an immigrant from China who came to the United States in 1988 and describes herself as a survivor of Mao's Cultural Revolution. Williams campaigns on a platform of immigration enforcement, limited government, and economic freedom, and has built a sizable online following.

candidates.name: Victor Orlando
candidates.summary: Victor Orlando is a Republican candidate running for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District. A business owner and tradesman from Hollis, New Hampshire, he positions himself as a political outsider with blue-collar roots. Orlando is campaigning on a platform of fiscal responsibility, limited government, and opposing federal overreach.

candidates.name: Robbie Mahrou
candidates.summary: Robbie Mahrou is an Independent candidate running for U.S. House in New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District. He is listed by Ballotpedia as a general election candidate for the November 3, 2026 election.

candidates.name: Dean Pennington
candidates.summary: Dean Pennington is a Democratic candidate who has filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission to run for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District. He is an analytics professional from Hudson, New Hampshire, and has not yet made a formal public announcement of his candidacy as of mid-2025.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast is based entirely on non-polling fundamentals. Incumbent Democrat Maggie Goodlander won the open seat in 2024 with 52%, a narrow 4-point margin. The district has trended Democratic but remains competitive. Goodlander benefits from incumbency, but the Republican field — including two-time past nominee Lily Tang Williams and primary challenger Victor Orlando — has not yet been settled (primary is September 8, 2026). A Democratic primary challenger (Dean Pennington) has also filed but not formally announced. Independent Robbie Mahrou is a minor factor. In a closely divided national House environment, Goodlander is a modest favorite given incumbency and the district's Democratic lean, but the lack of polling, narrow 2024 margin, and crowded primary fields keep confidence low. The tilt_d rating (55-64% Democratic win probability) reflects a narrow Democratic advantage with substantial uncertainty.
